root_cause.text: target_tg_pt_gp_members_show() in the SCSI target configfs code trusted snprintf()’s return value as the valid source length for memcpy() without clamping it to the 256-byte TG_PT_GROUP_NAME_BUF stack buffer, allowing over-read when long WWN/IQN names caused truncation.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (cur_len > TG_PT_GROUP_NAME_BUF || (cur_len + len) > PAGE_SIZE)` before copying, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that a 256-byte stack buffer was filled with `snprintf()`, whose return "can exceed the buffer size," so `memcpy()` would "read past the stack buffer and copy adjacent stack contents" because the existing check only protected the destination page.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a length guard in target_tg_pt_gp_members_show() to reject oversized group-name entries before they can overrun the output buffer.
intent_record.what: The buffer length check inside target_tg_pt_gp_members_show() was changed from only testing whether cur_len + len exceeds PAGE_SIZE to also testing whether cur_len itself exceeds TG_PT_GROUP_NAME_BUF before appending formatted output.
intent_record.how: At runtime this adds an extra bounds check on the per-entry formatted name length, causing the function to warn and stop before using an oversized group-name buffer entry, which helps prevent overflowing or mishandling unexpectedly long target port group names.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant function body is present in full: `target_core_alua_tg_pt_gp_show_attr_members()`. It declares a fixed-size stack buffer `unsigned char buf[TG_PT_GROUP_NAME_BUF];`, then formats into it with `cur_len = snprintf(buf, TG_PT_GROUP_NAME_BUF, "%s/%s/tpgt_%hu/%s\n", ...)`. Immediately after, it does `cur_len++; /* Extra byte for NULL terminator */` and then `memcpy(page+len, buf, cur_len);`. This matches the root cause exactly: the code trusts `snprintf()`'s return value as the source length for `memcpy()` without clamping it to the actual buffer size. If the formatted string is longer than `TG_PT_GROUP_NAME_BUF`, `snprintf()` returns the full would-have-been length, so `cur_len` can exceed the 256-byte `buf`, and `memcpy()` will over-read past the end of the stack buffer. There is no fix present here such as clamping `cur_len` to `TG_PT_GROUP_NAME_BUF - 1` (or similar) before copying.
